{"self_assessment": "Impact: I built the belly line, the full lower outline of the fish, from the start domino around to the middle crossing. The start's fall runs through this stroke, so it is central to the picture. I then took ownership of the nose joint, where the top line joins the run. I found why it wasn't catching (a sideways offset, plus one jammed domino) and bridged it. Before the push, about 108 of 111 standing dominoes were connected to the start. The only unconnected ones were three strays by the nose that don't affect the outline.

Execution: I laid the belly stroke from the pad in several builds, then used close inspections to check the chain. I traced the break to its cause, cleared the jammed domino and bridged into the pale section. After that I kept my hands off, so I wouldn't risk bumping a finished run. I checked the top line again afterwards and confirmed it was dark apart from the strays.

Collaboration: I told the table what I was working on and where, so no one else needed to touch the nose. I asked Jack to watch the top line and check the tail join, and Sofia to check the middle. I asked everyone to keep clear of the nose and middle in the final minutes, which reduced the chance of bumps.

Leadership: I took responsibility for the joint that was blocking the whole picture and kept updating the table until it was resolved. In the last stretch I helped the table settle on a hands-off approach and set a clear way to flag problems: shout and point at any pale stretch. That kept the finished fish intact until the push.", "my_share_percent": 30}
